#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination: a local directory path or a remote host:path (scp-style).
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"

[ -n "$DEST" ] || { echo "backup.sh: no destination (set BACKUP_DEST)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d logs ] || { echo "backup.sh: logs/ not found" >&2; exit 1; }

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

# If today's bundle already exists, add a time suffix so reruns don't overwrite it.
if [ -e "$BUNDLE" ]; then
    BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP-$(date +%H%M%S).tar.gz"
fi

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*|*@*)
        # host:path or user@host:path -> ship it over scp
        scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # local directory -> copy into it, keeping a unique name there too
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"
